title: Female borrowers requesting lower amounts of local currency may fund faster than those requesting higher amounts.
Female borrowers who express explicit thanks to lenders may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language like 'dreams' for their family's future may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a specific geographic location in their pitch may fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly describe themselves as single women may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who make a direct promise to repay the loan promptly may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention having previously received a Kiva loan may fund faster.
Pitches from women that employ standardized, repetitive, or generic phrasing to describe their work ethic or professional role correlate with slower funding speeds.
Male borrowers who express explicit thanks to lenders may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention the number of children they have may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Mentioning family obligations and benefits has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
Mentioning local currency amounts or specific institutional affiliations predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list the specific ages of their children fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their own age fund faster.
